\section*{Score-I papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S1-Q09, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=9, type=multi, subtopic={Doppler effect}, answer={A,B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: Doppler effect with wind | steps: effective sound speed relative to the medium for each wind direction; frequency formula and comparison with f1}]
Two vehicles, each moving with speed $u$ on the same horizontal straight road, are approaching each other. Wind blows along the road with velocity $w$. One of these vehicles blows a whistle of frequency $f_1$. An observer in the other vehicle hears the frequency of the whistle to be $f_2$. The speed of sound in still air is $V$. The correct statement(s) is (are):
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If the wind blows from the observer to the source, $f_2>f_1$}
\opt{B}{If the wind blows from the source to the observer, $f_2>f_1$}
\opt{C}{If the wind blows from observer to the source, $f_2<f_1$}
\opt{D}{If the wind blows from the source to the observer, $f_2<f_1$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S2-Q04, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Standing waves}, answer={2.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: energy in a standing wave | steps: mode number and time dependence of the phase; energy fully potential when cos(wt + pi/3) = +-1; second such instant gives 120 t0 | I: energy is purely potential at maximum displacement}]
A string fixed at both the ends of length 2 m, vibrating in its 7th overtone. Equation of the standing wave is given by $y=A\sin kx\cos(\omega t+\pi/3)$. All the symbols have their usual meaning. Mass per unit length of the string is 0.5 gm/cm. Given that $A=1$ cm and $\omega=100\pi$ rad/sec. If after time $t_0$ starting from $t=0$ sec, energy of vibration is completely potential for the second time. Find $120\,t_0$. (Use $\pi^2=10$)
\end{bankq}

\section*{Nurture SRG papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S1-Q04, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=single, subtopic={Sound waves}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: travel time of sound through air with a temperature gradient | steps: speed as a function of position; integrate dx over speed; substitute the linear profile; result}]
How long will it take sound waves to travel to distance $\ell$ between the point A and B if the air temperature between them varies linearly from $T_1$ to $T_2$? The velocity sound propagation in air is equal to $v=\alpha\sqrt T$, where $\alpha$ is a constant.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$t=\dfrac{\ell}{\alpha\left(\sqrt{T_1}+\sqrt{T_2}\right)}$}
\opt{B}{$t=\dfrac{\ell}{2\alpha\left(\sqrt{T_1}+\sqrt{T_2}\right)}$}
\opt{C}{$t=\dfrac{2\ell}{\alpha\left(\sqrt{T_1}+\sqrt{T_2}\right)}$}
\opt{D}{$t=\dfrac{\ell}{3\alpha\left(\sqrt{T_1}+\sqrt{T_2}\right)}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S1-Q05, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=single, subtopic={Waves on a string}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C2 F0}, diff_note={concepts: superposition of five waves of the same frequency | steps: resolve each amplitude into components; add the components; ratio of the sums; phase angle}]
Five sinusoidal waves have the same frequency 500 Hz but their amplitudes are in the ratio $2:1/2:1/2:1:1$ and their phase angles $0,\pi/6,\pi/3,\pi/2$ and $\pi$, respectively. The phase angle of resultant wave obtained by the superposition of these five waves is
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$30^\circ$}
\opt{B}{$45^\circ$}
\opt{C}{$60^\circ$}
\opt{D}{$90^\circ$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S1-Q06, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=single, subtopic={Doppler effect}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: difference in speeds of two cars from the reflected frequencies | steps: frequency reflected from a moving car; difference of the two frequencies; relation to speed difference; convert units}]
A stationary source is emitting sound at a fixed frequency $f_0$, which is reflected by two cars approaching the source (from same side). The difference between the frequencies of sound reflected from the cars is $1.2\%$ of $f_0$. What is the difference in the speed of the cars (in km per hour)? The cars are moving at constant speeds much smaller than the speed of sound which is $330\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}$.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{6.128}
\opt{B}{7.128}
\opt{C}{8.128}
\opt{D}{9.128}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S2-Q08, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=8, type=multi, subtopic={Doppler effect}, answer={B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: moving source and detector at an angle | steps: relative velocity along the line joining them; formula for the received frequency; time when it equals the source frequency; trend}]
A source of sound and detector are moving as shown in figure at $t=0$. take velocity of sound wave to be $b$.\par
\bfig{127.1}{NSRG03_p1_phy_s2_q08_1.png}
For the situation mark out the correct statement(s).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The frequency received by the detector is always greater then $f_0$.}
\opt{B}{Initially, frequency received by the detector is greater than $f_0$, and then decreases with the time.}
\opt{C}{Frequency received by the detector is equal to $f_0$ at $t=d\cot\theta_0/(2v_0)$.}
\opt{D}{Frequency received by the detector can never be equal to $f_0$.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S2-Q10, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=10, type=multi, subtopic={Waves on a string}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: speed of waves in a stretched string, transverse and longitudinal | steps: tension from the strain; transverse speed; longitudinal speed; powers of the quantities}]
Length of a string of density $\rho$ and Young's modulus $Y$ under tension is increased by $1/n$ times of its original length. If the velocity of transverse and longitudinal vibrations of the string is same, and the value of such velocity is $Y^a\rho^bn^c$, then:
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$a=-\dfrac12$}
\opt{B}{$b=-\dfrac12$}
\opt{C}{$c=-\dfrac13$}
\opt{D}{$c=-\dfrac14$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S3-Q04, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Doppler effect}, answer={6}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: extreme frequencies from a source moving on a circle | steps: condition for the maximum and minimum frequencies; tangent from the detector; positions of the source; displacement}]
A source is moving across a circle given by the equation $x^2+y^2=R^2$ with constant speed $v_s$ in clockwise sense. A detector is stationary at the point $(2R,0)$ w.r.t. the centre of the circle. The frequency emitted by the source is $f_s$. Find displacement between 2 positions of the source when the detector records the maximum and minimum frequencies. (given $R=2\sqrt3$m)
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P1-PHY-S3-Q05, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Standing waves}, answer={1.434}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: specific gravity of a stone from a sonometer wire | steps: tension with and without buoyancy; frequency ratio with length; solve}]
A stone is hung in air from a wire which is stretched over a sonometer. The bridges of the sonometer are 40 cm apart when the wire is in unison with a tuning fork of frequency 256 Hz. When the stone is completely immersed in water, the length between the bridges is 22 cm for re-establishing unison. The specific gravity of the material of the stone is (assume fundamental mode of vibration).
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S2-Q08, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=8, type=multi, subtopic={Waves on a string}, answer={B,C}, answer_src=solved, working={$y$ depends on $x+9t$: travels along $-x$ at 9 m/s; $T=\mu v^2=0.3\times81=24.3$ N; the amplitude is $2e^{-3}$}, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: pulse on a string from its equation | steps: identify the variable combination; direction and speed; tension; amplitude}]
A travelling wave pulse on a string of linear mass density $\dfrac{3\mathrm g}{\mathrm{cm}}$ is given by $y=2.00e^{-\left(4x^2+324t^2+72xt+3\right)}$ where $x$ and $y$ are in meter and $t$ in second then choose the correct options.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Wave pulse is travelling along positive x-axis with speed 9 m/s.}
\opt{B}{Wave pulse in travelling along negative x-axis with speed 9 m/s.}
\opt{C}{Tension in the string is 24.3 N}
\opt{D}{Amplitude of wave pulse is 2.00 m}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S3-Q02, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Standing waves}, answer={45}, answer_src=solved, working={Second harmonic at 30 Hz; next harmonic with an antinode at the quarter point is the sixth: $f=6\times15\times\tfrac12\times\tfrac12=45$ Hz}, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: frequency of a string in a higher mode with changed tension | steps: mode that has an antinode at the quarter point; frequency scaling with tension and mode; next mode; value}]
A string fixed at both ends with tension 100N is vibrating in lowest mode of vibration for which a point at quarter of its length from one end is a point of maximum displacement. The frequency of vibration in this mode is 30 Hz. The frequency (in Hz) emitted when it vibrates in the next mode with new tension 25N such that this point is again a point of maximum displacement is
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S3-Q04, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Sound waves}, answer={84.8}, answer_src=solved, working={$I=\dfrac{p^2}{2\rho v}=\dfrac1{3300}$ W/m$^2$, level $=10\log\dfrac I{10^{-12}}=84.8$ dB}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: sound intensity level from the pressure amplitude | steps: intensity formula; level in decibels; value}]
Calculate the sound intensity level in decibel for a sound wave travelling in air at $0^\circ$C and having a pressure amplitude of 0.5 Pa. Assume density of air = 1.25 kg/m$^3$, velocity of sound = 330 m/s, $\log_{10}(3.3)=0.52$
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=NSRG03-P2-PHY-S3-Q05, source={Nurture SRG - Test 03 (04 Feb 2024)}, paper=2, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Standing waves}, answer={3}, answer_src=solved, working={Air columns $0.6$ m and $2.2$ m give $\lambda/2=1.6$ m, $\lambda=3.2$ m; $0.6+0.6r=0.8$, $r=\tfrac13$ m, $x=3$}, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: resonance in a draining closed pipe | steps: air column lengths; wavelength from successive resonances; end correction; radius}]
A 5.0 long vertical pipe is filled completely with a liquid. A small hole is drilled at the base of pipe through which liquid starts leaking out. This pipe resonates with a tuning fork. The first time resonance occur when height of water column is 4.4 m and second time when height is 2.8 m respectively. If radius of pipe is found to be $\left(\dfrac1x\right)$m, find $x$
\end{bankq}
